subject: Event lead capture: scanner debounce and downstream tag mapping
messages:
From: Linda Hsu <linda.hsu@summitco.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: events@summitco.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Badge export -> HubSpot mapping + opt-in fallback

Hi Aisha,

We ran into a small wrinkle running last night's badge scan batch for Summit West. Some attendees scanned multiple times (badge tap retry on kiosks), and our current HubSpot ingest is creating duplicate contact activities and spammy lead owner rotations. Can Redwood recommend a debounce strategy that:
- dedupes repeated scans within an X-minute window
- preserves the most recent consent/opt-in flag if the attendee changes their selection on a follow-up form

We're also attaching the vendor's scanner export spec (CSV) and our current HubSpot ingestion rules. Main asks: recommended debounce window, canonical tie-breaker rules for consent, and whether Redwood can emit a downstream tag for 'manual-review' when vendor confidence < 0.7.

Thanks — Linda
Linda Hsu
Event Ops Director, SummitCo
(linda.hsu@summitco.com)

Attachment: scanner_export_spec_v2.csv

---
From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
To: Linda Hsu <linda.hsu@summitco.com>, events@summitco.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Badge export -> HubSpot mapping + opt-in fallback

Hi Linda — thanks for the detail and the spec. Looping in Ben (ingest/ops), Karthik (SF/HubSpot mapping), and Marissa (privacy/consent) to propose a concise plan. High level thoughts below; we'll follow up with a short playbook and config you can drop into your ETL.

Proposed quick wins:
1) Debounce: buffer identical badge_id hits from the same kiosk for a 3-minute sliding window by default; configurable per-event. Rationale: covers accidental double-taps without delaying real distinct interactions.
2) Consent tie-breaker: keep the latest explicit opt-in flag captured in any upstream source (kiosk form > QR followup > badge tap) unless the latest is blank — then preserve the prior explicit value.
3) Confidence tag: Redwood can emit a downstream boolean tag `redwood:manual_review` when the scanner vendor confidence < 0.7 or when required fields are missing. That tag can drive a HubSpot workflow to pause owner assignment.

Questions for you before we publish the ingest preset:
- Do you want debounce by badge_id only, or (badge_id + email) to handle shared badges?
- Are you using HubSpot dedupe by email or by external_id?

I'll draft the ingest-playbook and sample consent language. Ben — can you confirm the preferred CSV handshake (append vs upsert) and whether we should include an event timestamp rounding?

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Field Marketing Ops, Redwood Inference
---
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, Linda Hsu <linda.hsu@summitco.com>, events@summitco.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Badge export -> HubSpot mapping + opt-in fallback

Quick technical notes:
- Vendor CSV: prefer upsert semantics using `external_id` (badge_id) and event_timestamp in ISO8601. See column mapping in attached spec. If vendor can include `scan_confidence` (0-1 float) that's ideal.
- Debounce implementation: use a 3-minute sliding-window aggregator keyed on (kiosk_id, badge_id). Emit only the last record in the window but keep an `occurrence_count` field for analytics.
- Timestamps: round to second granularity. For multi-scan within window, the most recent timestamp becomes the representative event_timestamp.
- HubSpot handshake: Redwood will call the HubSpot Contacts API with upsert by `external_id` and set a custom property `redwood_scan_confidence` and `redwood_manual_review`. If HubSpot dedupe is email-first, we'll fallback to email upsert but still write the `external_id` to contact property.

Attachment: ingest-playbook.md (draft)

Ben Carter
Field Integrations Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, Linda Hsu <linda.hsu@summitco.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Badge export -> HubSpot mapping + opt-in fallback

Marissa here — brief on consent language and auditability:
- Use an explicit checkbox with the following copy at point-of-scan or QR followup: "I agree to receive product updates and communications from SummitCo and their partners. Read the privacy policy." Make checkbox default unchecked.
- Store source and timestamp of consent on the contact as `consent_source` and `consent_timestamp` (e.g., kiosk_form, qr_followup). Redwood will map those to HubSpot properties.
- For GDPR/EU events: include the purpose dropdown (product updates | event followups | partner outreach) and map purposes to HubSpot consent sub-properties.

I've attached sample wording (consent_language_samples.docx). Also propose a short rollback: if a later form clears consent (explicit opt-out), we do not overwrite with older positive values.

Marissa Cole
Privacy Program Manager, Redwood Inference

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
To: Linda Hsu <linda.hsu@summitco.com>, events@summitco.com, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Badge export -> HubSpot mapping + opt-in fallback

Thanks everyone — Linda, next steps from our side:
- I'll send the ingest-playbook and a config JSON you can drop into vendor ETL by EOD Friday. (Attachment: ingest-playbook.md)
- Default debounce = 3 minutes, keyed on (kiosk_id, badge_id). If you want shared-badge handling, say so and we'll flip to (badge_id + email).
- We'll emit `redwood_manual_review` when `scan_confidence < 0.7` and include `occurrence_count`.
- Marissa will provide final consent verbiage and mapping rules for HubSpot properties.

Linda — are you comfortable with the 3-minute default? If yes, we'll push the preset and test with a small batch on Monday.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Field Marketing Ops, Redwood Inference
